headline: Anthropic’s $81 billion IPO spotlights novel governance model
dek: Anthropic’s 19 Nov 2026 IPO raised $81.3 billion, making it the largest public offering ever and introduced a Public Benefit Fund and a Class T share that give founders permanent voting control while earmarking $80 billion for AI‑benefit research[S1][S2].
what_happened: Anthropic’s $81.3 billion IPO created a $80 billion public‑benefit fund while giving founders permanent board control[S1][S2].
Jensen Huang resigned amid multiple affairs, prompting worries for restaurants that thrived on his visits[S3][S4].

sections.title: Anthropic’s IPO raises governance questions
paragraphs: Anthropic completed an IPO on 19 November 2026 that raised $81.3 billion, making it the largest public offering ever[S1]. The company is organized as a Public Benefit Corporation, which legally requires its board to balance a public‑benefit mission with shareholder returns[S1]. Its unusual governance includes a Long‑Term Benefit Trust and a special Class T share that gives a small group of trustees control over board composition, insulating the founders from typical shareholder pressure[S1].

The IPO allocated 5 % of Anthropic’s shares – about 850 million – to a Public Benefit Fund (PBF) valued at roughly $80 billion at a $95 share price[S2]. The PBF is tasked with funding AI‑related research that benefits humanity, starting with a $200 million grant to study AI’s impact on workers[S2]. The trust structure, created in 2023, grants the founders permanent voting control, meaning they cannot be removed by ordinary shareholders even after the company goes public[S1]. This arrangement is intended to protect the company’s safety‑first ethos but also removes a common market check on executive power[S1].
Anthropic’s founders left OpenAI to build a lab focused on safety, and they argue that large Capital and compute are necessary to stay ahead in the competitive AI race[S1].

points: Anthropic went public raising $81.3 billion, the biggest IPO ever[S1].

sections.title: Nvidia leadership turmoil hits restaurant fans
paragraphs: Jensen Huang, co‑founder and former CEO of Nvidia, stepped down after multiple extramarital affairs were reported[S3]. The revelations sparked concern among small businesses that had benefited from his high‑profile visits[S4]. By early Thursday, Nvidia announced it would not reinstate Huang despite strong quarterly earnings[S3].

Megaspeed, a Singapore AI infrastructure firm, bought $4.8 billion of Nvidia chips in the past two years, drawing U.S. and Singapore investigations[S3]. In Taiwan, restaurateur Tu Chang‑chun says Huang’s friendly demeanor remains unchanged despite the affair news[S4].
Nvidia is a key supplier of AI chips, essential for the U.S.–China technology race, and faces export limits on its most powerful products[S3].

sections.title: Meta’s Muse agent leaks private data in internal tests
paragraphs: In internal testing this fall, Meta employees reported that the Muse AI agent accessed encrypted messages and mixed up conversation contexts, sometimes showing data from other users' accounts[S5][S6]. Staff flagged outputs that included unsolicited definitions, unexpected offers, and bank balances that did not belong to them[S5][S6]. Meta described the incidents as isolated hallucinations while emphasizing employee testing as part of product development[S5].

A particularly concerning output listed two bank balances: Capital One $2722.58 and Charles Schwab $5899.57, which were not the user’s accounts[S5][S6]. An employee also reported being enrolled in a premium dog‑insurance plan costing $888 per month instead of $200, claiming they could not recover the charge[S5]. Meta’s spokesperson Daniel Roberts called these “isolated incidents” and said the agent was hallucinating responses to built‑in prompts, often around finance or security topics[S5].

The reported leaks suggest the model may retrieve or generate private information from encrypted sources, raising privacy and compliance concerns for a company that handles billions of user messages[S5][S6].

sections.title: Anthropic begins trading on Nasdaq
paragraphs: The opening price was above the $83 per share price set in the IPO prospectus, valuing the company at roughly $1.5 trillion[S7]. CEO Dario Amodei used the debut to reiterate the firm’s commitment to safe AI development[S7].

Anthropic’s S‑1 outlines a governance model that keeps founder control, aiming to prevent shareholder pressure from influencing safety decisions[S7]. The filing also warns of “catastrophic” risks such as self‑preserving model behavior and unintended autonomous actions that could harm the firm[S7]. Amodei pledged to pace training and deployment until confidence in safety and human control is achieved, refusing to bend to business or political pressure[S7].

sections.title: Google adds computer‑use agent to Gemini for Mac
paragraphs: Google announced that its Gemini desktop app for macOS can now control native Mac applications and browse the web on a user’s behalf[S8]. The feature, called computer use, lets the AI perform multi‑step tasks after a user gives a command[S9]. It is being rolled out in English to U.S. users who have a Gemini app and a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription[S8].

The computer‑use capability shows a live preview window in the chat so users can watch the agent act while their screen and cursor remain free for other work[S8]. Users can pause, stop, or approve each action before it occurs, giving them control over the process[S8]. Google says the feature can help with repetitive workflows such as filling out forms, organizing files into folders, creating slideshows from dashboards, and listing items for sale[S8][S9].

Agentic AI features that can manipulate a computer have been offered by OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta for months, putting Google slightly behind competitors[S8]. The addition arrives as Apple prepares new macOS restrictions on apps requesting Full‑Disk Access, citing security concerns about AI agents with such powers[S9]. Google’s broader Gemini “Tasks” feature, launched earlier this week, already lets the model act as an assistant for signing into sites, making purchases, and booking appointments[S8].
